articles.title: Google Debuts SynthID Detector Tool for Flagging AI-Generated Content, but It's Far from Perfect
articles.summary: Google's new web-based SynthID Detector opens AI-content checks to anyone who signs in, flagging images, video, and audio from Google, OpenAI, Nvidia, or Kakao models. It misses AI content without a SynthID watermark, such as output from Claude, Grok, and Chinese open-weights models, and cannot tell fully generated media from AI-edited media. Without a universal watermarking standard across all major model makers, a reliable way to detect AI content likely will never exist.

articles.title: Smoother Design Collaboration and Navigation on Figma's Mobile App
articles.summary: Smoother collaboration and navigation arrive in Figma's mobile app through a page dropdown, a frame preview slider, and share links to the exact page or frame. Individual frames and images export to the phone with format and size options, and the app reopens exactly where users left off.

articles.title: iPhone Air 2 is coming, here's everything we know so far
articles.summary: Apple's second-generation iPhone Air is reportedly coming in spring 2027 with upgrades aimed at addressing several compromises of the ultra-thin original. A second rear ultra-wide camera will join the main camera, while a larger 3,500mAh battery and more efficient 2nm A20 Pro chip should improve battery life. Apple is also expected to add vapor chamber cooling, allowing the thin device to stay cooler and sustain performance for longer.

articles.title: On Being Anything Other Than a Designer
articles.summary: A year of trying to be anything other than a designer comes as the AI era proves unkind to human-centered designers, especially outside massive companies. Every company has people who absorb organizational mess, work that pays poorly, carries no title, and is sometimes called glue work. The answer is not another heroic generalist but building enough capability into teams to understand customer need, experiment technically, and stop solving problems twice.

articles.title: POV: AI needs mascots, and only humans can make them
articles.summary: AI companies are increasingly turning abstract technology into approachable characters, with mascots such as Muse, Dots, Claw'd, and Notion's animated face giving unfamiliar systems personalities people can understand and relate to. Anthropomorphism satisfies human desires for connection and predictability, while animation can turn a few simple shapes into a character that appears to think, hesitate, search, greet, and react. The strongest mascots become storytelling systems rather than logos with arms, requiring human skills such as observation, empathy, timing, humor, restraint, and a coherent sense of personality.

articles.title: The Convergence of Design
articles.summary: Products often converge toward similar forms as their purpose becomes clearer, technologies mature, and physical constraints, economics, standards, and competition narrow the range of practical designs. Software can converge even faster, as demonstrated by the rapid spread of chat interfaces following ChatGPT, while emerging AI hardware remains in an experimental phase of pins, glasses, earbuds, and pendants. Whether through functional optimization, market pressures, shared constraints, or simple imitation, successful forms tend to become increasingly alike until a change in purpose or technology opens new possibilities.

articles.title: Jev for Designers
articles.summary: TypeSafe's Jev answers choice, score, and yes-or-no questions with a probability for each option instead of writing text. Its training rewards honest probabilities over confident-sounding answers, giving designers the calibrated uncertainty design work needs, though it reads only text and takes questions literally. A new demo adds a maybe zone to HeyStefan's emoji sorter, where Jev parks undecided emoji from a pile of 166.

articles.title: Louise Laborie draws the lonely, cinematic and in-between parts of America
articles.summary: French illustrator Louise Laborie uses watercolor and charcoal to depict America's motels, highways, skate parks, and other transitional spaces at dusk, populating them with teenagers caught between childhood and adulthood to create quiet, cinematic scenes shaped by loneliness, music, memory, and imagined stories.
